clue.text: Time and motive required for crime

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a motive is the reason for doing something

explanation.surface: A detective's maxim: to prove a crime you need opportunity and motive.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is a serious criminal offence, so the answer is an example of a crime.

clue.text: Right to put in bananas I felt for this pudding

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means placing a letter inside the following word group
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters after it are scrambled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the letters of I felt rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook decides bananas are just right to put in this dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like a pudding ingredient, but it is slang for mad and scrambles the following letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a layered British dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream, so it is a kind of pudding.

clue.text: Former copper starts to set everyone free

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman sets about releasing all the prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as policeman alongside 'former', but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a duty is to free or release them from it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Psychiatrist women blame in film

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
W is the abbreviation for women
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: In a movie, a psychiatrist blames women for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but it means the thin plastic wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink-wrap is a tight plastic film sealed round goods by heat, so the word names a kind of film.

clue.text: Pleasant embracing husband in appropriate place

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping arms round, so one word encloses the letter that follows

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A pleasant wife hugging her husband where it seems right.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding your niche means finding the position that suits you, a place appropriate to your talents.

clue.text: Cuckoo saw tree top

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters that follow are put into a mad new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cuckoo is spotted sitting at the very top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like the treetop where the bird sits, but it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is any upper-body garment, and a sweater is a knitted example of one.

clue.text: Dummy on farm runs in silly cow races

indicators.note: in tells the solver to place a letter inside the jumbled group that follows
silly means foolish or confused, so the following letters are shuffled about

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the letters of cow races rearranged

explanation.surface: Farmyard nonsense: a dummy watches cows racing round the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a stuffed human figure set up in fields to frighten birds, so it is a dummy on a farm.

clue.text: Animal's lair beneath end of the garden

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means one part sits below the other in the column
end of picks out the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of the word
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: A fox's den lies hidden at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical Garden of Eden, so the name is the paradigm garden of Genesis.

clue.text: Clothes pianist packs for the theatre

indicators.note: packs means holds inside, so the letters sit within the words before it

parts.note: run across the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A pianist packs a suitcase of clothes before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespian derives from Thespis, the first Greek actor, and describes anything relating to drama or acting.

clue.text: Victor and loser set up, journalist decided

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
ED is short for editor, a crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A match was rigged, the winner and loser fixed, a reporter concludes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resolved means having firmly decided or made up one's mind; the past forms match.

clue.text: Suffer at home with bad dog

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
a cur is a bad-tempered or worthless dog; 'with' just joins

explanation.surface: Someone has a miserable time stuck indoors with a vicious dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer it, bringing it upon oneself; the two verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: Non-stop aces badly restricting Seles

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the preceding word come out jumbled
to restrict is to hem in, so one set of letters surrounds the other

parts.note: the letters of aces rearranged
Monica Seles, the tennis player, taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis report: an opponent serves aces relentlessly, keeping Monica Seles in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Monica Seles was a top tennis player of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ceaseless never stops, so the adjective is a direct synonym of non-stop.

clue.text: Long leases unusual in city

indicators.note: unusual suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters take an irregular arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Property news: lengthy rental agreements are rare in this city.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is the Californian city, so it is an example of the general word city.

clue.text: Attractive stone circle seen with friend

parts.note: the letter O is circle-shaped
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Visitors admire a ring of standing stones, accompanied by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone circle' reads as Stonehenge-type monument, but 'Attractive stone' is the definition and 'circle' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, prized for its beauty, so it is an attractive stone.

clue.text: Bouncer you hit to get in?

definitions.text: Bouncer you hit to get in?

parts.words: Bouncer you hit to get in?
parts.note: surface reading: a nightclub doorman you assault to force entry

parts.words: Bouncer you hit to get in?
parts.note: setter's reading: a bouncing object struck with a racket so it lands in court

explanation.walkthrough: A bouncer is a club doorman, but here it is anything that bounces; 'in' means landing inside the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a player strikes the bouncing ball and wants it to land inside the court lines, called in.

clue.text: Biden and Trump, say, sounding like excessively croaky people

indicators.note: sounding like tells the solver to judge the words by their sound when spoken, not by their spelling

parts.note: excessively means too much
a croaky voice is hoarse
a race is a people or ethnic group; spelt the same either way

explanation.surface: A jibe at two elderly presidential candidates whose voices are failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too hoarse race', said out loud, becomes an idiom for a contest with only two serious contenders.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2020 and 2024 US presidential elections were contests with only two real candidates, which is what the idiom describes.

clue.text: Hits down by 50% affected archery ranking

indicators.note: affected means altered or influenced, so the letters of the next word are changed in order
cut by half, so only the first part of the word survives

parts.note: half of the four-letter word, its first two letters
the letters of archery rearranged

explanation.surface: An archer's score falls by half, hurting their place in the rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is a system of ranking people or things one above another, so the noun matches.

clue.text: A decade passed in chains

indicators.note: in tells the solver to place one word inside the other

parts.note: ties are bonds or chains
went means passed, as time goes by

explanation.surface: Ten years spent shackled in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' reads with 'A decade' as time going by, but it gives a word to be placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties is a ten-year span, from twenty to twenty-nine or 1920 to 1929, so it is one decade.

clue.text: Not very encouraging sign from conductor

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the first beat of a bar, shown by a downward stroke of the baton

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign from conductor' might suggest a bus conductor; it is the orchestral one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pessimistic as an adjective and, as a noun, the stressed first beat marked by the baton.

clue.text: Maxim used by SAS, as her windows smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken into pieces, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Special forces storm a house, with the owner's windows shattered in the raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the motto of the SAS, so it is a maxim that regiment uses.

clue.text: Pool in 11? I don't believe it

parts.note: 11 across is a city, abbreviated to its initials; 'in' points to it
go on! is an exclamation of disbelief

explanation.surface: Someone reacts with disbelief to news of a swimming pool in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 11 across, whose initials stand for that city.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of still water cut off from the sea, a natural pool.

clue.text: Number one went first without kit on

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for urinating
whoever went first led the way

explanation.surface: The top footballer led out his team before changing out of his strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' suggests the champion or Pelé; it is nursery talk for a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeled, in informal British use, means stripped of one's clothes, so it means without kit on.

clue.text: A little mansion in Eaton Square

indicators.note: a little of something is only a small part, so the letters are a short stretch inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A modest property listing in Eaton Square, a very grand London address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eaton Square' reads as one place name; Square is the definition on its own. Eaton Square is an expensive street in London's Belgravia.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, so it is a square number; the definition gives an example of a class.

clue.text: Officer's given cold beer, getting notes in order

parts.note: a major is an army officer, with the possessive S kept
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An army officer is handed a chilled pint and gets his paperwork in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A major scale is a sequence of musical notes ascending in a fixed pattern, so it is notes arranged in order.

clue.text: Chick knotted towel

indicators.note: knotted means tied up and twisted, so the letters of the next word are tangled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman ties a towel round herself after a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chick' suggests a young woman in a towel; it is a baby bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, so it is a chick of that bird.

clue.text: Spot Liberal out of fashion

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so one letter is taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: style means fashion
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is spotted dressed unfashionably.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a kind of spot or pimple.

clue.text: I would clean it out, just the same

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters before it are put out of place

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that cleaning a room would make no difference anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical are exactly alike, which is the meaning of the phrase just the same.

clue.text: Island that's a ring

parts.note: taken as written
to toll a bell is to ring it

explanation.surface: A short description of an island shaped like a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface feels like a definition, since an atoll really is a ring of coral, but 'ring' here means to sound a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or chain of islets, a kind of island in tropical seas.

clue.text: French composer emptied tray, being full

parts.note: Erik Satie, French composer of the Gymnopédies

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is taken out, leaving only the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: only the outside letters of tray survive

explanation.surface: A French composer clears his plate and is satisfied after his meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiety is the state of being full after eating, so the noun matches the gerund phrase in sense.

clue.text: Tango separately, date having claws

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
doing something alone is doing it separately from others
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A couple dance the tango apart, the date turning out rather vicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Talons are the hooked claws of a bird of prey, so taloned describes a creature equipped with claws.
